### Module(s)

mini.icons

### Description

I may be missing something, but when using [mini.icons](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.icons) as a [lazy.nvim](https://github.com/folke/lazy.nvim) dependency in multiple places, setting up `mock_nvim_web_devicons` as an option seems to make sense.

Sure, I could configure [mini.icons](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.icons) in one place, but this approach makes it clearer that I am replacing [nvim-web-devicons](https://github.com/nvim-tree/nvim-web-devicons) with [mini.icons](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.icons).

Example:
```lua
return {
  {
    'romgrk/barbar.nvim',
    event = { 'FileType', 'VimEnter' },
    dependencies = {
      'lewis6991/gitsigns.nvim',
      -- 'nvim-tree/nvim-web-devicons',
      -- Proposed
      { 'echasnovski/mini.icons', opts = { mock_nvim_web_devicons = true } }, -- mock_devicons = true
    },
    opts = {
    -- ...
}
```

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the suggestion!

I don't see a huge difference between having this as an option or separate function which requires explicit call.

Also, as far as I know, 'folke/lazy.nvim' might do some dark magic in the case of dependency is mentioned in multiple places. I vaguely remember seeing somewhere that it "accumulates" all configurations which makes it possible to have `config` field set once in a dedicated 'mini.icons' spec. At least [LazyVim doesn't call `mock_nvim_dev_icons()`](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3ALazyVim%2FLazyVim%20mini.icons&type=code) in every place 'mini.icons' is declared as part of specification.

Closing as not planned.
